text_fidelity_a:
Logitech G13 Programmable Gameboard with LCD Display Pros:
-Easily programmed.
-Multiple game memory.
-Many, many keys = many, many programming options.
-Digital readout looks good and lets you know exactly what download you are using without reopening Logitech window.

Cons:
-Flat palm positioning is not very comfortable for gaming (and can't be adjusted). My hand tends to cramp due to its bad ergonomics when playing FPS games more than an hour.
-Keypad ergonomics are badly thought out. Key rows are positioned bowing UPWARDS (away from your fingers) instead of downwards, making quick initiation of pinky and index finger keys more difficult.
-G13 is a bit large and can't easily be slid aside when not gaming (not a big deal to me, but somewhat inconvenient).
-Friends tell me that Razer and Logitech downloads interfere with one another, so if you have a Razer mouse or keyboard this may interfere with your use of either.
-Keys are a bit too close together without easily discernible gaps in between. This too often causes my thick fingers to strike 2 keys simultaneously.
-Overpriced for what it offers.

Overall:
Programming=excellent. Ergonomics=horrible.
For me, the keypad layout and palm rest do not work together. They look like they should, but they simply do not. The device concept is quite good, but the ergonomics make it just too difficult to consistently access and manipulate keys for real-time gaming. Very disappointing to me because with Logitech's years of experience in peripherals this should put Nostromo to shame---it simply doesn't because of the badly positioned keys and faulty wrist/palm rest ergonomics.

Follow-up:
-Down from 2 to only 1 Star, and it should be ZERO Stars. This thing is good only for a paperweight to remind me of my wasted time and wasted money.
-6 months down the road and, while gaming, each and every one of my gaming profiles (I have 3) will spontaneously reset to the default profile on their own or, even worse, all the G-keys become unresponsive.
-Sometimes on computer start-up the LCD screen lights up, but no profiles appear, not even default, and no keys respond.
-Sometimes on computer start-up the unit never powers on.
-Logitech's updates do not fix the problem(s). I've deleted the entire gaming software setup and performed reinstalls ad nauseum with no permanent positive result. What's even worse is this: it acts fine for a bit after a reinstall, so you think you've corrected it, then it starts screwing up ALL OVER AGAIN.
-BIOS adjustments do not fix the problems.
-USB ports and motherboard are completely functional throughout my gaming (I've tested/monitored them as I play) and they perform perfectly as the gamepad and/or its software crashes on its own.
-It's only 6 months old, and 2 keys are mechanically non-functional (G20 and the button below the joystick). My Belkin Nostromo n52 lasted for almost 8 YEARS of gaming with no problems whatsoever, and I was gaming three times as much back then. I'd grown used to the G13 so I was willing to overlook the buttons, or blame them on myself, and work around this issue, but when the software/electrical issues began occurring quite regularly I'd run out of patience.
-Forums addressing these (as well as other) issues have found no answers or solutions, only make-shift quick-fixes.
-Numerous forums also share the information that this is happening across a variety and multitude of different computer systems/set-ups.
-Many other owners, myself included, have had additional problems with the G13 when it is used after a computer has hibernated/slept, but we all learned to live with this as one of its quirks. We now see this as an indicator of its many issues.
-Many other owners have said that the problems began occurring after 3 or more months use (I suspect that in my case this took longer as it is only occasionally used for gaming).
-Logitech customer support has denied any fault in these matters and still maintains that their pruduct and programming is NOT the cause of any of these problems, so their help line has been useless. Meanwhile, the price plummets as word spreads.
-Only thing that works for any of us is to constantly disconnect gamepad from its current USB port, reconnect it, and computer may recognize it...but this does NOT always work...sometimes requires reboot as well...and sometimes this doesn't work either...so gamepad is inoperative until it decides to come back on a reconnection or restart. This is a band-aid at best. I refuse to do this to my system over and over.

This thing is getting returned. I advise you to save your money and time by buying some other manufacturer's product.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech G13 Programmable Gameboard with LCD Display

text_fidelity_a:
Moshi AirFoil Screen Protector for Kindle Paperwhite, Kindle, and Kindle Keyboard (2 Pack) Even though I’ve had my various Kindles for years and never gotten a scratch on any of them, I thought it would be nice to have a screen protector so that I could feel more confident throwing my beloved Paperwhite in my purse and taking it on the go. I have also been reading with slightly dirtier hands since I have a new baby, so once again, the screen protector seemed like a good idea to keep it from getting mucked up with drool or whatnot.

The thing that sold me on this particular screen protector is that it makes the claim that it has a permeable surface, so air bubbles don’t get stuck under it during installation. I didn’t find that to be true. Maybe I did something wrong, but I needed to carefully apply it and I used a credit card to apply even pressure to get the bubbles out. Bubbles did not magically disappear nor were they any easier to get out, despite the claim to the contrary.

That said, this is no harder to install than a screen protector on your phone. It’s a bit of a pain, you have to make sure your cats aren’t anywhere nearby, and you have to have meticulously clean hands and very good lighting to make sure you don’t get dust or junk stuck underneath. But once it’s installed, it does exactly what it’s supposed to, and the screen is still very responsive. I really don’t notice it, beyond knowing that my screen is now protected.

Overall, though it doesn’t live up to the hype of being easier to install than other screen protectors, this is a perfectly serviceable product that does what it is supposed to.
text_fidelity_b: Moshi AirFoil Screen Protector for Kindle Paperwhite, Kindle, and Kindle Keyboard (2 Pack)

text_fidelity_a:
Ring Alarm 5 Piece Kit (1st Gen) – Home Security System with optional 24/7 Professional Monitoring – No long-term contracts – Works with Alexa The most popular review on here, Kyle’s from Oct 2018, has a lot of good points such as praising the system where it works right and suggestions for how it could be improved such as the need for a duress code.

The only major thing that review missed is the range extenders.
They are almost worthless.

If you read the reviews of the range extender when sold as a separate item you will read about some of the issues.

Issue 1: They are weak. People’s reviews and reviews from electronics publications find these extenders to be underpowered. There are many more powerful z wave range extenders in the market.

When I called tech support about this they blatantly told me they knew about the poorly performing range extenders.

They told me that some of the Ring compatible smart outlets made by other manufacturers, like GE, include range extended and that they work much better than the Ring range extenders.

At least the tech support person was honest in admitting that their extenders sucked and that compatible third party manufacturer extenders will work better...I guess?

There is a page on the Ring website that list all the Z wave devices made by third parties that are compatible with the Ring system.

Unfortunately you can’t buy the best reviewed and most powerful Z wave range extenders on the market because Ring does not make them compatible with their system because they want you to buy their crappy extenders of course.

I guess we should just be grateful that at least some of the compatible smart plugs have signal extenders built into them that are better than Ring’s.

Issue 2: They are dumb. The algorithms for determining what path a device takes, in terms of whether it connects to a certain range extender or the base station, is horrible. This flaw includes the range extenders themselves when they try and decide whether or not to connect to the base station or another range extender. (I have two Ring range extenders).

If you have one range extender 20-30 feet from the base station and then place another range extender 20-30 feet from the first range extender branching out in the same direction there is no guarantee that the second range extender will connect to the first range extender rather than trying to connect to the base station.

Maybe this is because the signal from the range extenders is so bad that the devices are programmed to connect to the base station if at all possible, even if the signal is weak.

One support tech even told me a “funny” story about how a friend of theirs has a range extender just fifteen feet away from the base station in their house and but the range extended chooses to connect to another range extender that is more than 40 feet away rather than directly to the base station that is just 15 feet from it.

Ha ha ha, it’s SO funny when your expensive electronic product that you bought to keep your home safe does not work correctly! Hilarious!

A secondary criticism is that if the signal to the keypad isn’t strong enough the keypad alarm might not sound.

I have two doors between my keypad and the range extender it connects to.
When the doors are open the keypad usually sounds the alarm, when they are closed it never does.

It would seem obvious to any rational person that the issue with the alarm not sounding is the signal strength but the tech support people swear up and down that that is not possible.

Even when the doors are closed the tech support people claim the keypad reads as having an adequate signals strength ( the tech support people can see the signal strength of your devices but you can’t).

They are actually sending me a new keypad but I am not hopeful it will solve the problem.
It seems obvious to me that the command for signaling the alarm requires a better signal than the other functions of the keypad.

Maybe the signal for the alarm is only sent out once while the signal for the other functions are repeatedly sent out until the base station acknowledges them? Who knows?

The point is that it seems like a design flaw and if you plan on having your keypad more than a room lengths away from your base station you shouldn't count on the alarm on the keypad working.

I will update this review with the performance of my replacement keypad.

The last thing I will say is that the price of 11 dollars a month for monitoring the entire system regardless of how many devices you have, including any cameras, is a great price.

I hope that this type of price is here to stay. If they pull a bait and switch where they significantly increase the price of monitoring after they initially get enough people to buy the system I will drop this system like a hot potato and sell it used on eBay.
text_fidelity_b: Ring Alarm 5 Piece Kit (1st Gen) – Home Security System with optional 24/7 Professional Monitoring – No long-term contracts – Works with Alexa

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin 4.3-Inch Carrying Case Bought this for the 750 because it didn't come with a case. A similar (smaller) case came with my 360 and I didn't think this purchase through. After using it and comparing the other cases out there, I would buy a different case.

This slipcase for the 750 fits tight. That's good. The Nuvi won't slip out. But because the 750's on/off switch is now a slider on the top left corner, if you slide it into the case naturally (unit in your right hand, case in your left) the switch rubs against the case. When you pull the unit out, it "automatically" turns on. Thus if you were to pull the unit out partially then push it back in, you could turn it on and not know it.

The solution is to invert the Nuvi so its switch will be at the open end of the case after it's in the case. That way you can see the switch's on/off position and verify it's not on.

More practical issues:

Pros:

- Nicely made: very high quality

- Very compact

- Adequate protection against rattling inside a glove compartment or briefcase

- Good basic case

Cons:

- It can accidentally turn the unit on

- It's black: can't find it easily in the dark buried at the bottom of my shoulder bag when traveling. Experienced this with the 360's case. And if it falls on the floor of a rental car at night, good luck trying to find it. Wish it came in natural leather color.

- Offers no protection while hand holding the unit while walking

The [[ASIN:B0012MI7N2 Garmin Nuvi 800 Series Carrying Case]] case is a wallet style that flips open to reveal the screen. It stays on the unit during use and offers some protection if you dropped your Nuvi on the sidewalk while walking. Downside with that unit appears to be that the cover flap does not latch, allowing the case to flip open in a briefcase and the screen to be scratched by other junk. And it's also black and can get lost on a car floor.

Another alternate is one of the many zippered semi-rigid or neoprene cases.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin 4.3-Inch Carrying Case

text_fidelity_a:
Belkin 8-Outlet AV Power Strip Surge Protector with 6-Foot Power Cord and 2 USB Charging Ports, 3000 Joules, Black (BV108050-06-BLK) I love that this surge protector and plug strip has two USB ports for charging my Kindle and cell phone, but the placement of the USB ports, which is a major selling point for this unit, is hindered by the position of the cord wrap feature as well as the areas to plug in your larger electronics that have the big boxy plug. The USB ports are tucked right in between the cord wrap spot and the place to plug in larger plugs, so if one isn't blocking your USB ports, the other is.

In addition, I kind of wish that the majority of the plugs were spaced farther apart. I have a few electronics that have very small boxy plugs, and those don't fit right next to one another on the main area of the plug strip. The only thing that will fit on those plugs without overlapping are the traditional small plugs that are on lamps and other uncomplicated items. I don't have too many of those, and I'm guessing that most people buy plug strips because they have a bunch of electronics, almost all of which would have those bigger boxy plugs.

That said, the surge protector feature is absolutely effective, and I know this because we had PG&E replacing some poles in our neighborhood recently and we had many incidences of brownouts, surges, and spotty power, and this unit kept any harm from coming to any of my electronics that were plugged into it.

And while it is easy to make design suggestions, I have to say that I haven't found the perfect plug strip yet. Almost all of them seem to have some design characteristics that make them not quite ideal. While this unit is not perfectly designed with regards to the placement of the USB ports and the spacing of the regular plugs, it is certainly a high-quality, very functional unit that does what it says it does, and I trust the Belkin brand that it's going to function for some time. This plug strip is also nice in that it has a space so that you can mount it on the wall or on the back of your desk if you so desire.
text_fidelity_b: Belkin 8-Outlet AV Power Strip Surge Protector with 6-Foot Power Cord and 2 USB Charging Ports, 3000 Joules, Black (BV108050-06-BLK)

OnePlus Buds Z2 True Wireless Earbud Headphones-Touch Control with Charging Case,Active Noise Cancellation,IP55 Waterproof Stereo Earphones for Home,Sport, Pearl White If you own OnePlus smartphone, these earbuds are easy to recommend. The budget-friendly $80 price matches the demographic that OnePlus has been cultivating. More importantly, some of the features of these earbuds only work with OnePlus phones. This includes Dolby Atoms and low-latency gaming playback.

Sound quality is clear, but very bass heavy. Unlike more better quality earbuds, these have no equalizer feature to help you get a more natural sound profile. Curiously, these earbuds do have the AAC CODEC for iPhones, but no aptX that Android phones prefer.

Noise cancellation is pretty good for this price range, though it does reduce your battery life somewhat. Battery life without noise cancellation is about average for the budget-price point, but not as good as what more expensive earbuds offer.

There is no wireless charging, though I'm not a huge fan of that anyway, especially for headphones.

I give 5 stars for OnePlus phone owners, but only 3.5 stars for everyone else.

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Oasis – With 7” display and page turn buttons- Ad-Supported + 3 Months Free Kindle Unlimited (with auto-renewal) I have never had an e-reader before. I used to read a TON, but then I grew up and life happened, so wanted to get back in to it.

I purchased both the Paperwhite and the Oasis. The Paperwhite seemed like a great device, but I could tell immediately how much more my eyes liked the larger screen on the Oasis along with the warmth feature. The warmth feature was the biggest factor for me, as it made it look much more like an actual page out of a book. I've included a picture of the Paperwhite (on the right) and Oasis (left), both set at the same brightness, but with the Oasis's warmth setting on. You can also see there is no white Kindle logo on the Oasis, which I found ever so slightly distracting on the Paperwhite. The quality of the screen on the Oasis is also much better than the Paperwhite - text is more clear and crisp. If you commute a lot or size is important to you, Paperwhite is definitely the way to go.

I was really overwhelmed with the Oasis at first, just because it was so new to me. I'm pretty good with new tech, but the whole environment was slightly overwhelming because it's not just as simple as getting a new device on a platform you're already used to (ie, Windows, Android, Apple, etc). Once I got past the learning curve, I started to actually like it a bit. However, the way the Kindle sorts and handles your books could be much better. You can organize things in to 'Collections', but it still doesn't feel like enough. I recommend looking up Calibre and going from there.

My biggest gripe is the ergonomics of the Oasis. Although it's not much heavier than the Paperwhite, it feels like it because of the shape of it. It just feels heavier because of the weight distribution towards the center, and is awkward to hold with that bump/excessive weight distribution that sticks out. I am a 5'9" woman with 'normal' sized hands, so I can't even imagine how this would be for someone with smaller hands. I bought a case immediately because the shell is ridiculously slippery, and in my opinion, a horrible choice of material for something you're going to hold for hours. Looks pretty, but not very functional for an e-reader. I bought the 'Ayotu Skin Touch Feeling Case', and it is awesome. I ordered a couple of others and this one stood out among all of them big time.

Last gripe is that the screen is pretty slow and laggy at times. I know it's an e-reader, but it's a very expensive one that doesn't do anything else (which to clarify I am absolutely fine with BUT, see next point), but at that price, it should really be perfect.

A positive feature of this that is nice is that you can flip the device around and the screen flips with you, so if you are right or left handed or just want to switch sides during reading, that is super helpful.

I do like it, but am considering whether or not I am going to keep it due to the ergonomics alone.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Oasis – With 7” display and page turn buttons- Ad-Supported + 3 Months Free Kindle Unlimited (with auto-renewal)

Michael Kors Access Gen 4 MKGO Smartwatch- Lightweight Touchscreen Powered with Wear OS by Google with Heart Rate, GPS, NFC, and Smartphone Notifications The MKGO has the best battery life of any WearOS watches I've tried. On a fairly busy day with the app running in the background on my iPhone the whole time, I was able to wear the watch from 6 a.m. until I went to bed around 10. The other three android watches I've tried didn't make it to dinner.

But this doesn't have a speaker.

Why doesn't this have a speaker?

One of the indispensable features of my Apple watch is being able to answer a call quickly when I have stepped out of the room my phone is in. I have lupus. I can't run. People somehow seem to know to call about something important when I've gone to the bathroom or stepped out to the mailbox. I'm close enough to be connected to my phone, but not close enough to answer it.

This never happens with spam calls. Just the ones from the people I won't be able to get back to through their nightmare phone menus.

The lack of this feature makes the watch unsuitable for me, and that makes me sad, because the iPhone is a begware spamming disappointment machine these days, and I really want to move to android.

The results are phenomenal. I'm now booting up in 20-30 seconds instead of 2-3 minutes. Programs like Word and Excel come up so fast (without any associated services running full time in the background) that you barely see the splash screen. I firmly believe a good SSD is the best thing you can do for a computer. 250GB seems to be the sweet spot right now as far as price goes (i.e., a similar 500GB drive will probably cost more than twice as much).

When cloning the a larger drive, you have to drag and drop all the smaller partitions over first, and then your C partition, which is probably your largest and with the most empty space. The program will then chop off the extra free space on the C partition, which is fine. Otherwise, you will lose any partitions logically after the C partition.

However, the performance of my computer slowly declined until I could no longer rely on the computer to not crash randomly within 30 minutes of starting it. Everything was failing. I could not figure out what the heck was going on. Started troubleshooting everything. Couldn't get through a memtest, so I bought some new ram so I can use my computer while I wait for the G.Skill RMA process. However, even with the new ram, the PC cannot boot with the Sabrent NVMe. Does not proceed further than the loading screen.

Tried booting into safe mode, which failed, as well as resetting the computer through the windows troubleshooting tool. Nothing would go past the loading screen. I've added another photo showing that substantial loss of performance, even while it is not being used by anything else. Keep in mind that although the numbers are mostly higher than the SATA SSD, a loss in performance like this is a tell-tale sign that it is failing. If you notice something similar with your hardware, back up what you want to keep immediately.

Tried booting from my older SSD, and was able to boot just fine. I am still somehow able to access the information on the NVMe when booting from another SSD, but the system is unstable while running on it. I will continue to try to get a replacement or a refund before conceding that I have a $120 tax for trying to save money.

I tried to use the tool to check if there was a firmware update. Doesn't work, as it said cannot find information on the hardware. This is with the latest everything. Seemed odd, so I sent an email to the bug reporting email they provide. Got a response from google saying that email does not exist....

I reached out to Sabrent technical support. No response after a week.

I'm very disappointed. I've gotten other sabrent hardware before and hadn't had problems. Looks like their memory is not their game. Even worse that their customer support is non-existent. Don't expect to get help if you run into the same issue that I got.

I'd recommend spending the extra $20 or $30 to get hardware that has a record of reliability, like samsung (the much older SSD that still works, and and using right now to be able to even use my computer is the 840 EVO).
text_fidelity_b: SABRENT 4TB Rocket NVMe PCIe M.2 2280 Internal SSD High Performance Solid State Drive (SB-ROCKET-4TB)

Pioneer Elite SP-EC73 Andrew Jones Home Audio Center Channel Speaker Atmos is the newest (at least at the time of this writing) innovation from Dolby. The idea is, rather than discrete speakers, the system packages sound into objects and has the speakers work together to play the sounds in the way that most recreates what is intended. So in theory you can have as many speakers as you want. In practice, the receivers will support but so many and people will want but so many in their living room. Speakers will always need to have some distance between them or the sounds will blur. The format allows for sound from all directions, including the ceiling and not many people are going to want to hang speakers from the ceiling, which is where a speaker like this comes in.

It has two input pairs, top and bottom. DO NOT plug in the top pair unless your receiver supports Atmos. You can damage it that way. If it does, you put the "upper" speakers into the top pair and these speakers fire upward to bounce the sound off the ceiling giving you the illusion of sound from above.

If you don't yet have Atmos, and you want to pick up great speakers now, and build up over time, you can totally do that with these. You plug in the bottom pair (these will be connected even with Atmos) and let them sit in any speaker position in your configuration. They work well in any standard configuration.

The sound quality is crisp and clear and the range in both pitch and volume is remarkable. The footprint is much smaller than the photo had led me to believe. It looks like an elegant piece of furniture. I love it.

You will need a Philips head screwdriver to put on the base. There are spikes to help balance it on a carpet, but mine lives on a hardwood floor, so I did not attach those.
text_fidelity_b: Pioneer Elite SP-EC73 Andrew Jones Home Audio Center Channel Speaker

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Basics Wireless Bluetooth Fitness Headphones Earbuds with Microphone, Black Short story of the review is that these are just as they say they are--a pair of relatively inexpensive "basic" earphones. As such, they seem to be a decent value and have some good points, but if you're looking for sound quality over price, you'll want to go elsewhere.

Pros:
Packaging: small and minimalist as it should be

Provided with: multiple size earbuds caps and ear inserts (more on these later), a very short charging cable, and a decent zip-around traveling pouch

Pairing: No problem with any of my Apple devices. Instantly recognized and paired with an iPhone (8 and 6), iPad (Pro and Air 2), and MacBook Pro. Couldn't be quicker or easier each and every time

Comfort: This was an issue for me, though obviously this is a pretty subjective category. I had to step down immediately to the small caps/rings, which is no surprise--I do that with I think all of my earbuds. But even with the smalls I just couldn't get a a good seal or a comfortable, though oddly enough much worse with my right. The left was not "great" but was certainly good; right was a bad seal and wholly uncomfortable no matter what I tried. Weird.

Sound quality: Again, it's a matter of pricing here. I don't own many basics and it's been years since I've had a set of lower-tier earbuds, so it's hard for me to compare at an equal level. The sound is what I'd call adequate, especially for exercise or listening to an audiobook. But there's no comparison to my PowerBeats3 or Jaybird X2s, and not even to my Jabra Elites, which I"d call my mid-range ones. The first two are in a whole other class in terms of range, sharpness, richness, and comfort, while the Jabras are a good step up in both sound and comfort. Sound here is more than a little thin at both ends, and just not very rich or full. Less noticeable with an audiobook, but definitely not the buds I'd choose if I'm focusing on listening to music, as opposed to having background sound while I"m doing something else. Phone quality is pretty similar--adequate, at times a bit muddy.

Controls: easy, intuitive, and responsive

Overall, if you want a basic set where quality of sound isn't a deal breaker, or a pair of cheaper ones for places you might have to worry about forgetting them, these will suit the bill, assuming you don't have the same comfort issue I did. But for someone looking for rich, full sound, particularly for music, I'd strongly advise moving up the ladder
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics Wireless Bluetooth Fitness Headphones Earbuds with Microphone, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Panasonic DMC-TS6A LUMIX WiFi Enabled Tough Adventure Camera (Blue) I’m a big fan of the Panasonic Lumix line of point and shoot cameras. I’ve been using one for years and, while it has limited features by today’s standards, it has yet to let me down. This latest one in the Lumix line offers a huge range of capabilities, provides outstanding image quality, but continues to suffer from a less than ideal user interface.

The camera comes with just the basics: the camera, a single battery, lanyard and a charger (plus manuals and software). I was a little disappointed right off the bat when I saw the charger. Unlike the older Lumix chargers that had a wall plug built into the charger than flipped out, this has a separate power cord. While that does make it easier to plug into the wall, it also means I have to remember to carry the cord with me to charge it.

Initial setup is straightforward, with the usual time/date setting. Since this has a GPS there’s also the need to go through initializing that option as well. All of these steps can be skipped, but you’ll be reminded to do so every time you power on the camera. It also displays a warning on screen about the waterproof limitations of the camera (and provides ample documentation as to what it can/can’t do re: underwater use).

The view screen is wonderful. Sharp, clear, and easy to read in all lightning conditions. The menu system will be familiar if you’ve ever used a Lumix camera but, if not, it’s still pretty straightforward. I still think Canon has the lead when it comes to having an intuitive point and shoot menu system, but Panasonic does a decent job. I like that with most options there’s a scrolling line of text that comes up to explain what the option is/does. That’s very helpful for options you don’t often use and need help with, but it does not interfere or slow down operation should you know exactly what you want to select.

I won’t list all the camera specs in this review since those are easily available in the listing and the Panasonic web site. Suffice it to say this offers a huge range of options and capabilities that cover pretty much any shooting situation. The Intelligent mode shooting scenario options (of which there are many) are helpful when you just want to point the camera and have it do everything else for you, including compensation for specialized lighting/scene situations. I especially like the macro option, which produced some impressive close-up shots that were sharply focused and clear even though I didn’t use a table-top tripod for stability but relied on the image stabilization features of the camera.

The video recording image quality is excellent good for a point and shoot cam. The performance of the built in mic is decent as well. This won’t compete with a dedicated HD cam, but for casual video shooting it’s a small, simple and easy to use setup that gets the job done pretty well.

The WiFi setup was surprisingly easy. I was dreading that since it often can be a bear, but this was quick and easy, and the included instructions were easy to follow. I use the WiFi option a lot since the USB port to connect to a PC is inside the camera (located under the battery compartment door). It’s done that way to maintain a water-tight shell, but is also means it can be hard to get to easily.

What has not been improved, and actually has slipped a bit, is the overall user interface (e.g., the buttons on the back). They continue to be small, hard to read, and don’t provide solid feedback that they have been pressed. Given that the camera is designed to be used in “rugged” conditions, larger buttons would have been a big plus, especially for zoom and the main menu keypad since those are used so often. Using the menu buttons is hard enough with bare hands; it’s impossible if you have gloves on.

I would certainly recommend this camera if you’re looking for a rugged point and shoot for outdoor use, but also if you’re looking for a high feature camera that never leaves the house. The performance and feature set are both excellent. The user interface brings my rating to four stars but performance and option-wise, this camera offers a lot for the price point.
text_fidelity_b: Panasonic DMC-TS6A LUMIX WiFi Enabled Tough Adventure Camera (Blue)

Kindle Wireless Reading Device (6" Display, U.S. Wireless) I am probably one of the least intuitive people around when it comes to technology. I've bought quite a few gadgets that have ended up collecting dust as I never really learned to use them properly. My short lived relationship with a Palm Pilot ended in frustration when I didn't learn how to back it up on my PC and all my carefully inputted data was lost (more than once!) My kids use it now for a doodle pad. My husband says I have a "black thumb" when it comes to anything electronic. If there is a way to break it, lose it, or misuse it, I'm right there doing it. This is why it is so astonishing that I have grown to love my kindle 2.

I learned how to use it easily within a few minutes. It is so intuitive- my four year old enjoys it and can page back and forth reading classics such as George MacDonald's The Princess and The Goblin or Mary Pope Osborne's The Magic Treehouse. My tween age son uses it for Shakespeare- I downloaded the First Folio (35 plays from the Bard) for all of 99 cents! It's quite a favorite amongst my children and I have recently learned that if more than one family member has a kindle, all e-books may be shared with a single purchase. My friend can even access her kindle books and magazines from her iphone!

Cool features include 6 different options for font size, and text markers by "location" to bring you to the same line of text whether you use the biggest or smallest of fonts, as page numbers would vary too much to be useful. A male or female voice can read to you, though the voices are a bit stiff and robotic, and they make small mistakes such as using alternate pronunciation that don't fit context with heteronyms such as read/read or live/live. You can connect speakers or earbuds/headphones for this feature. Magazines can be downloaded as a single issue or a subscription, but the subscriptions cannot be canceled from the kindle- the user must go to amazon's "Manage my kindle" area to do this.

I have downloaded quite a few classic books for free and spent about a dollar on many others. So far, the younger children's literature has been somewhat limited, but I imagine that as prices drop, more will become available. I am a bibliophile and I never thought I would love a paper book replacement, but this device is so clean and glare free that I forget I am not looking at a paper page.

I'm sure that color kindles will be available within a few years, to make the illustrations a bit more interesting. I love the beautiful pen and ink type renderings which fill the kindle 2 screen when it isn't in use. Obviously though, color would be more attractive with other types of art. Black and white is easiest on the eyes for text, and mostly that it what kindle is all about.

The kindle 2 holds a charge for a long time. I think I plug mine in about once every couple of weeks. If you are not careful with the five way button, sometimes you do end up getting the wrong result. I purchased a book accidentally this way, but amazon has a handy "did you purchase this by mistake?" option which permits you to cancel the order if you act right away.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Wireless Reading Device (6" Display, U.S. Wireless)

text_fidelity_a:
Acer Aspire R 15 2-in-1 Laptop, 15.6" Full HD Touch, 7th Gen Intel Core i7, GeForce 940MX, 12GB DDR4, 256GB SSD, R5-571TG-7229 This will be a fairly detailed and honest review.

1. Who is this for?
This computer is what I would consider a gateway computer. Those who are looking at upgrading a fairly old or not so powerful laptop and are looking to do a little more productivity, this is a great option.

2. What do you get?
Well you can probably read the description, however it's worth noting. You get an Intel i7 7500u CPU (dual core with 4 threads) 12gb DDR4 RAM, Nvidia 940mx GPU, a 256gb SSD, 15.6" 1080p screen, fingerprint reader, and a backlit keyboard.

The reason I mention all of the feautures is because you would be hardpressed to find another laptop with these features for the same price. To my knowledge there is not laptop on the market for $800 with an i7, dedicated graphics, 12gb of RAM and an SSD. This is really one of the best values on the market right now.

With all of that said, this isn't for everyone. If you want to do extensive gaming, this is not for you. Can it game? Yes, light gaming can be achieved, however it isn't marketed as a gaming laptop. Is this for someone who wants to do editing (video, audio, photos)? Yes, again light editing can be achieved.

What blew me away with this computer is the speakers! They are fantastic! I usually use headphones and would consider myself somewhat picky with sound, and for laptop speakers these are really something great.

This computer is really a middle of the pack all arounders dream. If you dabble in a little of this and a little of that but don't do anything professionally or extremely serious, this is really all you need.

Also, everyone's experience is different. Some hate loud fans, and if this is pushed the fans will be audible. Some don't like that the backlit keyboard times out after 30 seconds of no use. These things really don't bother me.

Lastly, the versatility of this laptop is really great. I've bought tablets and sold them because I couldn't justify having a laptop and tablet, then bought tablets again because I missed the things I could do with them that I was missing on a laptop. This solved all of those issues except size. It's pretty big, which for some is a plus others its not.

Overall, if you are looking at upgrading and don't want to spend $1,200-2,000 on a flagship model laptop this is a great option! I can't recommend this enough.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Aspire R 15 2-in-1 Laptop, 15.6" Full HD Touch, 7th Gen Intel Core i7, GeForce 940MX, 12GB DDR4, 256GB SSD, R5-571TG-7229

text_fidelity_a:
Maxell Full Size Illuminated Keyboard CkI-1 This keyboard works pretty well. Good amount of resistance in the keys, and it has lasted me almost two years. It is just now starting to lose accuracy in one of the shift buttons.

Pros: Has lasted fairly well. Keys are lit enough to make viewing easier without being too bright. Convenient hot keys. VERY convenient mute key is the top right corner where it is easy to find quickly. A little "clacky" but not super noisy. Few accidental letter presses. Build quality is pretty good.

Cons: The enter key is according to a non-US layout. The \ button is right beside the enter, and it took me about a year to stop accidentally typing a slash. If you are used to this layout it is fine, but do be aware that it is not the standard US keyboard layout.

Other: the volume knob is very handy, though after a year and a half it mysteriously fell off... not sure if it was misused by my kids or if it was spontaneous.

Bottom line: it's a good build and it should work for you if you prefer this (international?) keyboard layout over the standard US keyboard layout.

Valkit for New iPad Pro 12.9 2017 Cover, iPad Pro 12.9 Case, Apple iPad Pro 12.9 Inch 2015 Folio Smart Folio Stand Protective Heavy Duty Rugged Armor Cases with Apple Pencil Holder, Black This is a decent lightweight case for your iPad Pro, and it’s a good value-for-your-buck. However, I wouldn’t trust this to be your ‘durable case’, say for traveling, commuting, distracting the kids. I am concerned that a fall with this case may cause significant damage, especially as the case ages. I’ve had the case for quite a few months now, and the first thing I can note is that the PVC screen cover is very loose, and needs to be carefully placed when closing it, so that it covers the screen completely. I am no longer able to use the folded screen cover for propping the tablet up anymore, because of the wear.

On a happier note, the case *IS* easy to remove, so you can use a heavier and more protective case when you need to travel. This case adds almost no weight to the tablet as well. The colored part of the PVC hasn’t scraped off or cracked either. So, as a light weight, safe-for-home case, it’s a solid 4. As an ‘all purpose’ case, I’d rate it a 3 on it’s own, or 3.5 if you’re putting it into a computer backpack with a padded chamber for it.

text_fidelity_a:
Kodak PlayFull ZE2 Waterproof Video Camera with 2x Optical Zoom and 2-Inch LCD Screen (Black) I made absolutely sure everything was closed before putting it into water, not that one could have much faith in the mechanisms keeping it closed, as they are easy to accidentally open. I put it in the water gently, and only a foot or so, to film some stingrays and fish; this recording went fine. Later that day, I wanted to photograph a tiny little crab. I took one picture from above the water, and one from below. I noticed this time, when I put the camera underwater, that bubbles started to come out the top. I immediately took it out and noticed the screen starting to fog up with condensation and moisture, the first very bad sign. I double checked everything was still closed, and it was. No part of it had been opened. I put it back in, hoping for the best. After coming back to the sand (never having done more than a few feet underwater), I tried to turn it on to get some video. It would not turn on. I checked again, and nothing appeared to be open. I then dried the exterior and opened it, only to discover there was water on the inside. I immediately removed the SD card, in hopes of salvaging it, but the camera was (is) completely dead.

Two days later, there is corrosion forming on the inside from the water, but at least I salvaged the content on the SD card. The results? Video quality is fine above and below water. Photo quality is a mess. Absolutely the worst pics imaginable.
I am so glad I didn't have to pay for this product; I would have been furious it didn't even last a day in the ocean.

I expected more, since I had previously purchased a "Kodak EasyShare Sport C123 12 MP Waterproof Digital Camera", which has been great! That product never failed after much abuse and takes decent picture and video. I'm not sure what happened here, but buyer beware! Try the EasyShare Sport instead.

I'll post some pictures and, if it lets me, some video too. I hope you all find this helpful!

UPDATE: I can't post video (sorry)
Also, I looked at some other reviews that mentioned water getting in while at the pool or in other non-salinated water. Bear in mind that many electronics can survive water immersion if it is fresh water (as opposed to salt water). Many of these reviewers gave the camera more than one star because it was able to work again, but bear in mind this will NOT hold true it Salt water enters the device. Please consider this.
text_fidelity_b: Kodak PlayFull ZE2 Waterproof Video Camera with 2x Optical Zoom and 2-Inch LCD Screen (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Harmony 900 Rechargeable Remote with Color Touch Screen (Discontinued by Manufacturer) First let me start by saying I am an IT professional and have been a audiophile and video hobbyist for many years. Naturally I have had a lot of different audio / video equipment over the years. I had a computer hooked up to my TV long before it was in fashion. And finally, I am always looking for the next great gadget on the market. Enter the Harmony 900.

Here is my current setup in my living room:
Samsung TV HL-T5687
Sony PS3 Move
Nyko IR Adaptor for PS3 - Media Hub Slim
Roku2 XS
Onkyo TX-NR808
Sharp DVDR-VCR DV-RW340
Cable Box Motorola DVR DCH-3416
Shuttle PC with Media Center
X10 Home Automation - Various Devices

I basically use my TV as a monitor, the only cable plugged into it is the HDMI from the receiver. Hence, the Onkyo receiver does all the sound and switching between inputs.

The Harmony 900 Experience:

I did a lot of research before buying this $250.00 remote. Considering this thing is 50.00 more that my Kindle Fire and does a whole lot less, it wasn't easy pulling the trigger.

Ergonomics:
I read the good and bad reviews and decided that this one would best fit my needs. From many of the negative reviews I concluded the biggest concern was going to be dropping it and breaking the screen. It becomes very obvious why this is the minute you put it in your hand. It is very sleek and conforms well to your hand, but is as a slippery as a fresh water eel in your hand. Also due to the few contact points with any surface other than the charger, it is very easy to slide off a couch arm or get bumped off a coffee table.

That being said, the remote is very well balanced and fits nicely in the hand. The buttons are raised and easy to push. However some of the buttons are simply in the wrong spot. The volume and channel buttons should be reversed and the "Menu" button should be located down further on the remote. The fast forward and skip buttons are perfectly positioned and the skip buttons have a notable bump on them to differentiate between the two.

The screen is actually better than I thought it would be. I can make out the display with or without my (fulltime) glasses. On the down side, it is very easy to tap on the wrong display icon when moving left and right through the screens. When this happens, depending on what you accidentally pressed, it takes a while to recover and get back to what you were watching. Some things may have turned on or off and if you weren't pointing in the right direction during the errant tap, good luck getting everything synced again.

Device Support:

The Harmony 900 claims thousands of supported devices. But good luck finding some of them. Instead of having a simple model number look up, you first have to choose the type of type of device, then the manufacturer followed by the model number. The problem is some devices are not listed in the device type or seem to be randomly added to device types you would not expect them in. There is an example in the set section below.

One thing clearly missing is a simple list of all the devices. In some cases like the X-10 IR interface module listed in many of these reviews, it is no longer available. It would be great to just enter X-10 and see every device that was compatible so you could buy the right one as an interface with the Harmony. There is no way to do this. This is a glaring omission that seems very simple to correct. Heck, a downloadable PDF would be better than nothing.

But all that said, I found every device in my house in their database and I had some fairly obscure AV stuff. And as long as the device is IR, you can custom map from any remote to the Harmony, so there really isn't any IR that cant work.

Setup:

Now I wasn't bragging when I said I was an IT professional. I simply mentioned this fact so those who are technically challenged have a baseline to consider when evaluating their ability to use and set up this device. I have built servers, computers, configured high end routers and switches and oversee hundreds of devices in several locations. And it always amazes me when I get a new piece of equipment like this, how frustrated I can get in the first few minutes of using it.

As others have mentioned, you have to install the software and set up an account to use the device. All settings are done interactively and in real time through the internet. If you don't have an internet connection, don't bother with this remote. I did not use the CD but instead downloaded the latest version from the Logitech web site. I also pre downloaded the owners manual several days before the remote arrived and read it cover to cover. So by the time I had it in my hand I was fairly comfortable with how the setup process should work. The software and driver installation was very easy and there were no USB connection problems to the remote. So far painless!

After letting the remote charge for a couple of hours I started through the setup process. I had used my own version of their worksheet and had all the devices written down. The first thing to note, again as other have mentioned is the Sony PS3 requires an add-on device to translate the IR to the Sony's native RF. Although Logitech sells such a device for almost 100.00, I already had a Nyko Media Hub for the PS3. It doesn't have all the functions of the Logitech, but it was only $17.00 and does all I need. And best of all, the Harmony 900 has the Nyko in it's database. The Roku2 XS is mysteriously placed in the DVD section and if I hadn't read some of these reviews I would not have known that. All the other devices mentioned above were in the database and all were added without an issue.

Once all the devices were added the software prompts you to add activities. Activities are the heart of the 900's functionality. However you must understand the concept of "Activities" and how they work to really get the most out of this remote. In a nutshell, an Activity is started by pressing a single button or in this case an icon like "Watch TV" . When you press Watch TV, the TV turns on and switches to the proper input, the Cable box turns on, the receiver turns on and switches to the proper input and output, and finally the 900 becomes a remote for all of those devices at the same time. More on this later.

To get a feel for this device I decided I would first set up all my devices without any activities. Essentially I wanted to just have a remote and be ability to go to one device after the other and see if they worked correctly. At first the software stumped me and didn't appear to let me get past setting up activities. I gave up trying and set some of them up thinking I could always wipe the remote clean and start again. I am not sure where I went wrong but the first activity I set up, "Watch TV" didn't work out so well. The TV didn't turn on, the Cable box turned off, etc. I ran back and forth from my PC to the living room about a dozen times and finally gave up for the night after about 2 hours of head banging. That night I re-read the manual, had the whole next day to ponder and went at it again .

The next morning I deleted all the activities and created them on my own, not using the wizard. I created an Activity, added the devices and then one by one told the software what I wanted each device to do. This was very helpful. I realized this not only got me the expected result, but it made me see how this software and remote really worked. After playing around for about 30 minutes I was able to create several of my most frequent activates. Going back to the equipment I pressed Watch TV. Again the TV did not turn on. If I used the Harmony for that device directly it worked. Back to the PC and set the activity to turn on the TV first. Still no luck. Next I tried the activity and used the on screen help. It asked if the TV turned on, I answered no and presto the TV turned on. After selects "this fixed my problem" on the remote, it worked every time. But; after each change on the PC I had to go through this help processes. I still do not know what the Harmony is doing to correct this.

Once I got all the basic Activities working I found a few other glitches. When I wanted to watch my combo DVF/VCR and use the VCR portion, none of the commands worked. It turns out this device has separate and distinct commands for FF-VCR and FF-DVD. The Harmony set all the DVD commands to that Activity by Default. I simply created two activities, One Watch VHS and one watch DVD even though it's the same source. In fact I found creating different activities for the same source is the answer to everyone complaining about missing the macro feature. It really does the same thing.

Now that I was on a roll my last bit of programming was renaming the activities. If you want the rest of your family to know how to use this thing without a PowerPoint presentation and tutor, I suggest you name the activities in such a way that its very obvious. Examples are Watch TV, Watch Netflix, Use PC, Listen to iPod, Listen to Pandora, etc. Since my receiver has an iPod dock, the Listen to iPod activity changed the source from whatever it is on to the receivers iPod port and then shows all the different music listening modes on the soft buttons. Watch Netflix switches to my Roku, etc.

Now for the best part of the Harmony setup! Its the ability to have the remote on the "Watch TV" activity and being able to program the hard and soft buttons to any other device's remote function. No more switching to the specific device's remote to change an often used setting on that device. If you take your time, you will eventually never have to use the "Devices" soft button as all the things you do will be setup in the Activity you are in. Now this takes some time and trial and error, but it's a huge time saver. Here is an example: You are Watching TV, controlling the sound options and volume with the Receiver, changing channels with the DVR and changing the aspect ration with the TV all on the same keypad. But beware! You can set what buttons do what on the device settings, but that won't change what they do in an Activity. The remote buttons MUST be set up in the Activity to work properly.

I spent several more days fine tuning the remote and now have not touched it in a while. I have a few more tweaks I am thinking of doing. And I would love to find the glitch that makes the TV turn on after I make any updates to the remote. Maybe a call is in order before my 90 days runs out.

USE:

As mentioned above, the ability to have the most common functions for several devices on one remote mode at the same time is huge! Now that I have used it for a couple of weeks, I have gotten accustomed to the button layout and can operate it without looking at it for most basic functions.

When everything is off and you select Watch TV, everything turns on and goes to the right inputs etc. However starting an activity can take quite a while. The remote can not be used while the Activity is being implemented. In my case I am already watching TV with sound on and the remote is still spinning the hour glass for a while. If you have the TV on too loud, you have to wait until the Harmony is done thinking or walk over and turn it down manually. However once that first activity is complete, any subsequent activity is changed fairly quick.

The battery life seems a bit short. I used to change the batteries in my remote once a year. This thing needs to be charged almost every day. If you let it go dead, its time to break out the old remotes during a recharge.

Once set up properly the Harmony 900 is very easy to use and the rest of the family had no problems with it, well almost.

Wife Problems:If your wife, child, etc. has a habit of turning the TV and other equipment on and off manually, you are in for some headaches. Since the Harmony remembers the last state of your devices (if you use it exclusively), it may turn things on instead of off, or off instead of on if someone else manually did that. My wife figured out the remote very quickly they way I have it set up. But she still does a mixture of using the remote and manual power buttons which frustrates both of us. Of course she blames the remote for not working properly when this happens. However anything that takes some blame from me is more than welcome.

RF Setup:

One of my misconceptions about this remote was the boasting of RF (Radio Frequency) capability. IT does indeed have IR capability. However, it does not have a database of RF codes like it does for IR codes. This device will not replace "ANY" RF remote, period. I was hoping there was a RF option for my X-10 home control devices, but that is not the case. For setups like this you need to get a IR to RF converted for the devices you already have. Figuring out which one you need can be a daunting task (See Device Support above).

The only RF device the Harmony will control directly is the IR blaster that comes with the device. An additional IR blaster can also be added. By default the IR blaster emits all the signals the remote puts out through IR to any and all blasters you have set up. You can control which blaster gets which signal. But this can only be done at the remote, not in the software. I am not sure why this is, but it is one of several deficiencies in the software.

Overall:

I went from wanting to return the Harmony 900 within hours of taking it out of the box, to protecting it like it is one of my children. I really love the Harmony 900 and would recommend it to most people. Those with little patients or difficulty working the microwave should avoid it unless someone else can set it up for you. It's overkill on a simply setup, like DVR and TV. But it is a pure joy if you have a medium to complex setup like I do. At $250.00 it is very pricy and hard to justify for a remote. But it seems to solve all my remote issues and to me it's worth it. I give it 4 stars.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Harmony 900 Rechargeable Remote with Color Touch Screen (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Fujifilm FinePix T300 14 MP Digital Camera with Fujinon 10x Wide Angle Optical Zoom Lens (Black) For the non-professional photographer looking to get high-quality images in a variety of settings, this camera works great. I did a little experiment to see how it performed by taking it with me to Europe along with a much more expensive semi-professional Nikon (D3100). Here are the results:

Advantages:
-With our limited time, my camera was able to take a variety of shots (panoramic, zoom, close-up) quickly and easily while the Nikon could only take limited kinds because of the need to bring several lenses and because of the complexity (sometimes) of setting up a given shot
-Because it was small, I didn't have to lug around a big camera bag, which also had the potential of getting a little too much unwanted attention
-One feature I really enjoyed was the two simultaneous flash/no flash shot which gives you the same picture with and without flash, letting you choose later which you prefer
-Didn't need more than one lens
-With city shots of architecture, my camera fared better with its versatility

Disadvantages:
-In the mountains, the Nikon did better, capturing color and clarity/detail. In my shots, the trees looked less defined from high up. Also, his zoom lens was able to capture much more detail than my camera.
-Nature shots and portraits have slightly duller colors, missing something the other camera was able to capture
-There was slightly more blur in shots with movement with this camera

Conclusion:
For the price, this camera performed much better than I expected and was not as much of a hassle as our semi-professional camera, so for most people, this is not only going to be a better value, but less frustrating and cumbersome. For the professional, this is obviously not the best choice, but this isn't being marketed as a professional camera. This is a great family and vacation camera that everyone can use, and that still yields quality images with plenty of artistic integrity.
Great little camera, and fun to use!

**see pics for some examples of how this camera performed**
text_fidelity_b: Fujifilm FinePix T300 14 MP Digital Camera with Fujinon 10x Wide Angle Optical Zoom Lens (Black)

Winegard FL-55YR FlatWave Amplified Razor Thin HDTV Indoor Antenna (Renewed) I bought the amped FlatWave refurbished because it was $25 cheaper than a new one, and I am quite pleased with it. It DID come with gunk on it from where the previous owner had taped it up, but the gunked-up side (the black) was the one I placed against the window, facing outside, where nobody is going to see it anyway.

We live in an apartment complex on the outskirts of a city with another apartment building sitting right in front of us where the antenna would face the closest transmission tower. The first time I scanned for channels, I just laid the antenna flat on the table next to the TV. I got 14 channels on that scan (the networks often transmit more than one, so those were ABC, NBC, CBS, and Fox with their variants, one of which was CW). I moved the antenna to the center of my window, which I didn't like the looks of, and got 20 channels when I rescanned, three of which were PBS variants I hadn't gotten before; the rest were shopping channels that I don't care to receive anyway. I moved the antenna over to the side of the window with the cord side up close to the edge of the sill so the cord would hang up against the wall and not look ugly, and I got 17 channels; all I lost were those shopping channels.

We have cable in our bedrooms but none in the living room, so that's where I set up this antenna. I'm hoping I can convince DP to drop cable at some point, because it's ridiculous how much we're paying for it. We could afford to travel some if we could cut back to just internet. But sometimes you just want to be able to watch TV....
text_fidelity_b: Winegard FL-55YR FlatWave Amplified Razor Thin HDTV Indoor Antenna (Renewed)

1MORE Dual Driver BT ANC In-Ear Headphones Wireless Bluetooth Earphones with Active Noise Cancellation, ENC, Fast Charging, Magnetic Earbuds, Microphone and Volume Controls, Silver I returned these because of a software bug with ANC - and also because the call quality was terrible.

These phones stood out for being wireless with active noise cancellation (ANC) AND pass through (so you can hear ambient sounds for safety in the City). Unfortunately, those features are the weak points of the headphones - to the point that I found I would never use the pass through and often didn't bother with the ANC.

SOUND QUALITY: VERY GOOD - EXCEPT - they tend to exaggerate the mid base a little which can make vocals - especially male vocals sound a little unclear. Listening to the same music on speakers vs the headphones, it was just plane more real sounding and pleasant on good speakers. High standard, I know. Other headphones don't have that particular problem (though may have others - like weak bass or sibilant highs). I haven't heard that many competing models, so I don't know how they compare to sennheiser or bose or anyone else in the same price class. At least others have an app with equalization (Jabra, Jaybird).

Bug w. ANC: Sometimes it would say it's on when it's off and vice-versa.

ANNOYING THING: When you engage the pass-through, it has a voice prompt that tells you the pass through is engaged. Since often I switch on the pass through when it's important to hear something, the several seconds it takes to make its silly announcement means I miss part of what I was trying to hear! I found I would always just yank one plug out of my ear instead and get the instant feedback. ALSO - this thing takes FOREVER to turn off. You have to hold hold hold and finally it announces it's powering off. Combined with poor power indicator light - this is just annoying.

NOTE: This is not a defect, but just poor design... There is NO WAY to activate Google Assistant or Siri with These. Even my cheapo earbuds let you use one of the buttons to summon Google. Without that, how are you supposed to make voice calls? I have to pull out my phone to make calls. Foo.

Combined with atrocious call quality (I could hear them, but the person on the other end is always mishearing words or saying WHAT? WHAT?), these are DOA for me.

ONE LAST THING: The APP is garbage. Just pointless.
text_fidelity_b: 1MORE Dual Driver BT ANC In-Ear Headphones Wireless Bluetooth Earphones with Active Noise Cancellation, ENC, Fast Charging, Magnetic Earbuds, Microphone and Volume Controls, Silver

The downside to using it with the original Fire is that you need to provide your own cable from the charger to the Fire, as the charger does NOT include it.

Using the app Battery HD to measure charge time and level, the new charger saved about 15 minutes to go from a 15% charge to a 100% charge versus the original charger. Faster, but not a huge gain. I expect that the differential in terms of charge time for the new Fire (especially the 8.9 inch one) will be much greater when comparing this charger with using a USB port to charge. I'll post results once I have my 8.9 inch Fire.

While it's not a compelling purchase if you have the original Fire, it is worth getting (at 50% off) if ordered with a new HD Fire, especially if you can also get the MP3 credit. DeLUX Ergonomic Wireless Vertical Silent Mouse - 2.4G USB Receiver, 3 DPI Levels (800/1200/1600), 6 Buttons, Removable Wrist Rest for Laptop PC (M618Plus Wireless-Black) Like most of us, I spend a lot of time working on the computer. I’m also picky about mice, but am trying to be as ergonomic as possible in my peripheral choices, to prevent problems down the road. My current daily driver mouse is Logitech’s MX Master 3 and I use a palm grip.

I’ve wanted to try a vertical mouse since reading about them, but for me, the DELUX Vertical Mouse won’t be the one. The mouse is just too big for my small hand. To give an idea of my hand size, I wear a size small women’s glove.

My hand doesn’t fit naturally on the mouse. My whole hand slides down the body, so I have to keep tension in my hand and arm to keep my fingers in the proper place to be able to use the mouse buttons. It’s not comfortable; my hand and wrist hurt within minutes. My thumb keeps sliding to sit on the bottom of the side buttons, so it’s fortunate for me the side buttons don’t work on Macs.

I tried the mouse with and without the palm rest, there was no difference.

On the plus side, the mouse charges via USB-C, and can connect via Bluetooth or wireless. If you don’t use it, the wireless dongle fits neatly into the base of the mouse without impeding using it.
text_fidelity_b: DeLUX Ergonomic Wireless Vertical Silent Mouse - 2.4G USB Receiver, 3 DPI Levels (800/1200/1600), 6 Buttons, Removable Wrist Rest for Laptop PC (M618Plus Wireless-Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Pogoplug Series 4 Backup Device Pogoplug (this and other models) are an inexpensive way to have some capabilities of more expensive Network Attached Storage (NAS) devices. The most significant difference is a Pogoplug does not come with a hard drive installed. You have to supply your own hard drive as the backup drive. Mostly, I don't recommend this device, or the other offerings in the product line. The Pogoplug is just the beginning of what it will cost to get a complete backup solution with remote access and cloud storage. It's a solution sold piece-by-piece and, in the end, for the same outlay you can buy systems with better functionality and more builtin features.

If all you want is a way to backup files from multiple computers running different Op Systems (e.g. Windows and Mac OS X) to a local backup system, the Pogoplug will do that. If, however, you want to access your files when you're away from home or the office where the Pogoplug is installed, you'll need to buy their app for that from the Pogoplug website.

If you want your files also backed up to cloud storage, you have to buy that as well from the Pogoplug website. They sell 1TB storage, although it's advertised as 'unlimited' cloud storage. In my opinion their cloud storage is expensive. Consider also it takes a very long time to upload 1TB of content and, should you decide to discontinue the service, it takes a lot longer to download that same 1TB.

The best way to think of a Pogoplug is that its like candy dispensing machine. You buy a Pogoplug (the machine) and get one piece of candy free as a promotional item. You purchase more candy one piece at a time. They sell a lot of candy and It's not cheap.

There are some things I like about this item and more I do not. For example, unless you're a big customer, tech support is only available by email. It takes a couple days for a question to turn around and for that and other reasons I don't like email support. Then, too, in order to get all the features I want is an expensive proposition, since the real meaty features cost extra. While Pogoplug Backup (the app that comes with the device) works on both PCs and Macs, it has an annoying glitch on the Mac platform. Whenever a computer restarts (often with all the software updates and service packs) Pogoplug software restarts as well. On the PC, this does not trigger a full backup of already backed up files. On the Mac it does. Essentially, the Pogoplug Backup app for Mac doesn't seem to keep track of what' been backed up so you get to work on a slowed down Mac while Pogoplug needlessly does a full backup. Further, while Pogoplug Backup updates files that have been altered, it does not have versioning.

The most frustrating thing about Pogoplug is that your files are stored on the device locally, on your local network. You'd think it possible to connect directly to the attached drive to access shared files. Not so! Access to files stored on your own drive, located in your own home or office are only available to you from other computers when logged into my.pogoplug.com through their interface. Think how you'll enjoy this when your internet connection is down or their site is down or a myriad other things get fouled up!
text_fidelity_b: Pogoplug Series 4 Backup Device

Kindle Oasis E-reader (Previous Generation - 9th) – Graphite, 7" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi), Waterproof, Built-In Audible, 32 GB, Wi-Fi - with Special Offers (Closeout) I purchased one of these 9th generation Kindle Oasis. The first unit I received would freeze during the configuration process. You could reset it, but if you try to configure, it would freeze again. At this point, I made the mistake of asking for a replacement instead of just returning the faulty Kindle Oasis for a refund. A replacement unit arrived in three days. Unfortunately, the replacement unit was DoA. There was a fixed image on screen, and I wasn't able to get a response from this Kindle after charging it for a long time and multiple reset attempts. I had already shipped the first unit back using a UPS shipping label created by Amazon at this point. I went to my Amazon Orders page to return the second unit for a credit. But Amazon web interface wouldn't allow a self service return for refund. I had contact customer service and deal with several customer service representatives. They consistently asked me to try some simple trouble shooting steps ( most of which are not even applicable if you have a completely dead kindle). They wouldn't listen to me when I said I just wanted to return it, and try to pressure me into another replacement. At this point, I had spent several hours troubleshooting, talking to Amazon Customer service, taking packages to UPS, etc. so I insisted on a return for refund. This time, the customer service representative said he was having problems generating the return label, and then disappeared. After several minutes of wait, another customer rep took over and worked on this case for another 10 minutes or so. At that point, I ended up with two sets of return labels in my email. The customer service rep told me to use the labels from the second email (in chronological order). So the next day, I shipped the replacement Kindle Oasis back. A few days later, I saw on UPS tracking that the package was delivered to Amazon and three days after this I received an email confirmation from Amazon that my first return was received. A few days later, I saw on UPS tracking that the second Kindle Oasis (replacement) was also received by Amazon. I waited a few days for return confirmation and refund from Amazon, but nothing happened. When I contacted Amazon Customer service, they kept telling me that I shouldn't worry about getting charged as my replacement is complete. But they could see no record of my return of the replacement. I spent probably a good half an hour chatting with a customer service rep but they couldn't help me at all since they could only see the record for on return request. That chat ended with no resolution because I ran out of time and had to get to an appointment. Later, I got in touch with yet another service rep, and explained everything from scratch. Luckily, that person was able to find records of both returns being received by Amazon and finally issued me a refund.

So lessons from this story:
1. Don't buy a 9th gen Kindle Oasis. There seems to be serious quality control issues. The probability of one customer receiving two faulty Kindles in a row would be infinitesimal unless fault rates are in the 20% range.
2. If you receive a faulty Kindle from Amazon, return it for a refund. Don't ask for a replacement. Amazon's automated return process cannot handle the return of a replacement unit, and you will sink a lot of time dealing with customer service representatives
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Oasis E-reader (Previous Generation - 9th) – Graphite, 7" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi), Waterproof, Built-In Audible, 32 GB, Wi-Fi - with Special Offers (Closeout)

text_fidelity_a:
Canon 6558B003 EOS Rebel T4i 18-135mm is TM Lens Kit 18MP SLR Camera with 3-Inch LCD Body (Black) I had been borrowing a T3i for the times when I wanted something more lightweight and portable than my 5D Mark II. Given all the time I was spending with the T3i, I thought it was time to get my own.

I was torn between the T3i and the T4i but Amazon made it easy since they were both priced the same before Christmas. So, I went for the T4i, and am very glad I did. It's a nice improvement over the T3i.

The most telling upgrade has been the touch screen. I admit I was a bit wary of this since I'm comfortable with the traditional buttons, menus and rocker switches. After using it for a few days I very much miss having it on my other Canons. Very responsive, allows me to jump to a setting more quickly, and just plain easy and fun to use!

I do have to admit that Canon's claim that this is a "smudge resistant" screen is only partially true. It sort of, kind of resists smudges, but I usually end up cleaning the screen a few times during use.

The other novel feature of the T4i is the ability to have continuous autofocus in movie mode. I'm more of a still photographer than a videographer, so that's does not make a huge impact for me. However, I have used it and it does work very well - I may start shooting more video now, and am considering getting the 40mm STM lens (although the continual autofocus works with any lens, it's best suited with an STM lens).

Most of the specs of the T4i are identical to the T3i; a few have been tweaked, such as a higher frame rate, higher ISO and faster processor.

I was a no-brainer for me to get the T4i when it was priced the same as the T3i. But now that I've had it for a while, I certainly think the added features make it a worthwhile choice over the T3i even at a higher price. It you purchased a T3i recently, it's probably best to wait for the inevitable T5i whenever it comes out rather than upgrade now. But, if you're debating between the T3i and the T4i, go for the 4, if only for the touchscreen.
text_fidelity_b: Canon 6558B003 EOS Rebel T4i 18-135mm is TM Lens Kit 18MP SLR Camera with 3-Inch LCD Body (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Amazfit BIP smartwatch by Huami with all-day heart rate & activity tracking, sleep monitoring, GPS, 30-day battery life, Bluetooth (Kokoda Green), One Size June 7, 2018—This watch, an Amazfit Bip smartwatch, arrived today so I'm posting an initial review about it. I come back after some time and change or add anything that needs it.
----------------------------------
Amended June 15, 2018
I have downgraded the Amazfit Bip Smartwatch from 5-Stars to 1-Star. This is why:
1) My Pixel 2 updated to Android 8.1, the watch unpaired in the process and now will not reconnect (pair with) the phone.
2) Nothing in Amazfit's on-line support addresses this issue. However, there are a significant number of Bip owners discussing this problem on the internet, outside of Amazfit's site.
3) The watch is not a useless brick and exchanging texts with Amazfit's tech support is not going to get this fixed (if at all) in a timely enough manner for my purposes.
4) Finally, I got 7 1/2 days service from this watch and that is very poor, indeed.

Sorry to say, my opinion is the Bip does NOT WORK WITH ANDROID 8.1. That seemingly the case, what will happen when Android P, now in Beta, releases as Android 9 in August, 2018?

I'm going back to my iPhone/Apple Watch. Yes, that combination has glitches as well. However, support for Apple Products is always reliable and you're not stuck texting for help.
text_fidelity_b: Amazfit BIP smartwatch by Huami with all-day heart rate & activity tracking, sleep monitoring, GPS, 30-day battery life, Bluetooth (Kokoda Green), One Size

After dithering for a couple of weeks, I finally took the plunge and ordered the kindle the day before surgery. I had a small satchel (guy purse) to carry wallet, kindle and phone with me when in therapy. My arms were too weak to hold the book I had with me. Friends brought my kindle to me the 3rd day. I then read about 5 to 6 hours or more a day and night. Charging was fast and I had no issues with battery life. I charged once a day. If needed I could read while kindle was charging. I bought the 3g and wi-fi addition. Downloaded on both as hospital wi-fi quit sometimes at night. Holding a book to read had become a chore for me some years ago. Sitting at a table reading was uncomfortable, therefore I have neglected to my reading. I have downloaded Edgar A. Poe's works. I especially enjoy his comic and scientific pieces. (See high school English classes ruined Poe for you, didn't it? It did for me until I discovered his other writings.) I downloaded some other large and heavy in print books. I am angry at self for not discovering the kindle and amazon book experience before now. I own some 3,000 volumes of history, science, etc. Very little fiction, except for Poe, Shakespeare, Twain, Doyle, and their ilk interests me. I don't read popular novels at all. I was surprised at the number of books and editions available for free or almost free that covers my interests. I don't consider myself as a snob for not liking popular fiction, it just doesn't interest me. But reading is a mind expanding activity, whatever one reads. It doesn't matter what you read, just do it.
I am 77 years old new kindle reader. Thanks amazon.
