Tram 1185 Amateur Dual-Band Magnet Antenna I bought this Mag-Mount antenna initially for my Boafeng UV-5R+ radio after I bought a SMA-to-SO239/PL259 Connector and I was hitting repeaters over 25 miles away at 5 watts. Later I bought myself a Kenwood TM-281A mobile unit for my car an for the moment it is in use there until I figure out what kind for permanent (drill-in) antenna I want to get for my car. Problem is, this Mag-Mount antenna works so good I am debating on if I really need to get a permanent. Now there are compromises to Mag-Mounts, like cable may not be too long, etc. Eventually I will get a drill-in antenna.

For the TM-281A I have two TX power settings, 65 and 25 watts. This antenna works on both but I couldn't find any documentation on the max power for this antenna so I normally just keep it a 25 watts and it still gets out there just fine.

I would caution to tape around the area where the cable connects to the Mag-Mount to keep moisture out. I haven't have problems yet but I hear that it can be a problem for just about any mag-mounts.

For this price, buy it, test it and if you don't need it, then keep it as a backup.

73'
K9RUM
text_fidelity_b: Tram 1185 Amateur Dual-Band Magnet Antenna

The range on this lens takes you from a decent wide angle perspective to a mid-range telephoto without any light loss (the maximum aperture is constant throughout the zoom range) and image stabilization keeps focus problems due to hand shake well away.

Optical quality is excellent, as you would expect with an L lens, and autofocus is smooth and fast. Keep in mind on a camera with a cropped sensor (any Canon DSLR model other than the 5D and 1D models) the focal range is equivalent to @40-170mm - you lose a bit of the wide angle advantage, but you get more telephoto, so it depends which end of the focal range you value the most as to whether that is a disadvantage or not.

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Wireless Anywhere Mouse MX for PC and Mac, black To be honest, I'm really tired of these mice failing.

They work great at first, then eventually quit scrolling or, worse, get stuck in scroll mode and drive the cursor to the bottom of the page for no reason. Two have failed on me. The first was purchased in 2011 for $36, the second in 2014 for $30. Both failed to scroll reliably and made using them impossible. Other, cheaper, wireless mice work better, or at least longer.

This mouse has nice features like left/right scrolling by tilting the scroll wheel and they work on many different surfaces, but those features fall by the wayside if the thing doesn't work at all after some time.

I've tried blowing it out with compressed air to clear debris, but it didn't fix it. Haven't come to taking it apart and cleaning it, as some proffer, because it's simply not worth the time.

For how much these mice cost -- $66 for the two -- they should be bulletproof. Better to buy cheaper wireless mice and throw them away when the fail.

I could have purchased six of them for what I've put into Logitech MX Anywhere mice, both of which become landfill fodder.

Logitech has lost my Anywhere MX mouse business.

text_fidelity_a:
Seagate FreeAgent GoFlex Desk 1 TB USB 2.0 External Hard Drive STAC1000100 (Black) Very pleased with the drive. Installation was truly plug and play - it took longer to get the drive out of its packaging than it did to install. Not often that you can say that with regard to a PC product!

The speed running on a USB 2.0 connection is very good. I didn't run any formal time tests, but it copied megabytes of files just as quick as any other external drive I've used. I can't comment on the backup software since I use a program that I wrote myself.

I love the fact that this can be upgraded to USB 3.0. None of my PCs presently have that option, but I expect the next one will and it's good to know that this drive can take advantage of the extra speed. Unfortunately, that's an extra cost item, but still far cheaper than having to get a whole new drive.

The drive enclosure is stylish (well, as stylish as a PC component can be). Quiet when running, and I'm pleased that the indicator lights are not the lighthouse beacon-style that seems to be in favor these days. You can see them, but they are not distracting.

I've been using Seagate external drives for years and have never had a problem - they just keep on ticking no matter what. In addition to this model I have a portable GoFlex (320 GB) that has been running nearly 24/7 for the past two-plus years without even a hiccup, and a non-portable 250GB that has been running for about seven-plus years, again with zero problems. Amazing that the 2 TB model is actually a wee bit smaller than the six year old 250 GB model!

Hoping that this model will continue the streak of zero failures with my Seagates. Highly recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Seagate FreeAgent GoFlex Desk 1 TB USB 2.0 External Hard Drive STAC1000100 (Black)

Canon EF 70-200mm f/4 L is USM Lens for Canon Digital SLR Cameras I upgraded to this lens from the non-IS version of the 70-200mm as I was having problems getting sharp shots not affected by hand shake. The lens is rather long and heavy and the image stabilization comes in quite handy, especially with shots under low light conditions when you don't want to raise the ISO too high to compensate. The IS can generally get you 2 stops more light than what you might ordinarily expect before experiencing hand shake blur.

Images from this lens are very nice - sharp and good color, good bokeh at the wider apertures so you get nice separation between subject and background. I took this lens to the zoo once and got lots of good shots with it, I've been very pleased with its performance.

I use this lens on a full-frame camera, so keep in mind that if you are buying this for a camera with a cropped sensor, the actual focal range is more like a 110-320mm.
text_fidelity_b: Canon EF 70-200mm f/4 L is USM Lens for Canon Digital SLR Cameras

text_fidelity_a:
Behringer MICROAMP HA400 Ultra-Compact 4 Channel Stereo Headphone Amplifier,Silver After an attempt to use [[ASIN:B005INJ4ZG My Zone Wireless Headphones]] was a bust for me due to its terrible sound quality, my techie husband bought this amp for me as part of a setup that allows me to listen to TV as loud as I want without disturbing him or the neighbors.

I directly hook up this amp to a head phone or earbuds when I am sitting close to the TV by using a special [[ASIN:B00009UVPN adapter]]. Head phones and earbuds have a 1/8 inch (3.5 mm) male jack (AKA male connector). Without an adapter, they can't be inserted into this amp, whose plug (AKA socket, female jack, or female connector) measures 1/4 inch (6.35 mm).

Because I like to move around my living room when I am watching TV, my husband also bought me a special [[ASIN:B0010CX798 male-to-female, headphone adapter, extension cable]]. The 1/4-inch, male jack of this cable fits into the 1/4-inch plug of this amp, and it has a 1/8-inch plug on its other end into which the jack of a head phone or ear bud can fit.

In order to use this setup, my husband also hooked into this amp a [[ASIN:B000068O3F male-to-male extension cable]]; one end is 1/8-inch and the other is 1/4-inch in diameter. The smaller end fits into a plug on the TV. When I want to use this external speaker source, I use the TV remote to access a menu that allows me to do that. Once this system is hooked up, I can no longer adjust the sound volume on the TV itself. I use the volume control on this amp.

Note that there is no On/Off switch on this amp. If you want to turn it off, so that you are not wasting electricity when it is not in use, you unhook the power cord from the far-left side of the amp.

This setup is a little complicated for the non-techie to figure out on their own, but if you have anyone techie in your family who can do it for you, it works really well.
text_fidelity_b: Behringer MICROAMP HA400 Ultra-Compact 4 Channel Stereo Headphone Amplifier,Silver

Ring Video Doorbell 2 with HD Video, Motion Activated Alerts, Easy Installation Another reviewer mentioned these issues, but I was impulsive and bought it anyways. They are all true.
- I spend a good deal of time adjusting the sensibility settings and using the brackets (both V and H) to reduce false positives, but they are still too many. My door is about 25-30' from the road and if a truck passes, even small cars, "motion detected". You stop giving importance for the sensor.
- I try to answer motion but it takes so long to load (I have an S8, with good wifi) and I got a connection problem way too often. If wasn't another false positive (as usually is), I would have missed the person lurking.
- The recording starts too late. when you go see the recorded video (because you were not able to answer the false positive motion), the video starts way too long after the movement started.
- regarding payments: I have a Piper camera that records up to 1,000 24s videos for free, overwriting after that. It works great. It always worked. Why Ring enforce additional payment is mind-blowing considering what is available on the market.
- I have installed with battery, that was really good because it was easy to install, but on the current pace (75% after 25 days) there is no way it will last the suggested 6 months on the website.

UPDATE: had to completely disable the motion sensor, the false positives were driving me crazy. Not paying the monthly fee. It's too many clicks to get to the screen when somebody actually pushes the button.
Avoid this product and wait for competitors to come up with something better.
UPDATE 2: Now this piece of crap will not enter live view.

text_fidelity_a:
Ring Video Doorbell 3 – enhanced wifi, improved motion detection, easy installation Great wireless camera/doorbell. Hardware/software this is ideal. We live on a busy street so we were getting lots of notifications. The software allowed us to adjust where the camera sensed motion, cutting down "false" notifications. Easy to use.
Easy to setup and install. Took maybe 15 minutes from opening the box to having it up and running.
Convenient set-up and access via phone (iOS and Android) app. Added skill to Echo, so when someone sets of camera or pushes doorbell, we get a notification via Alexa, and an image on the Echo show. You can adjust how often and what notifications you receive in the app.
Night vision is pretty good as well. Another nice feature is you can access a "live" view anytime, notification or not.
Audio works well, so if you are in the basement, garage, at work, shopping you can talk to whomever is at your door.
If you carry your phone everywhere or have a smart home speaker (Google, Echo or maybe Apple?) you won't need the additional chime, phone and speakers have a decently loud sound.
I would suggest getting a second battery if you have a busy street or lots of activity. The app notifies you in plenty of time the battery is low and needs to be recharged (only takes a couple hours to fully charge). But a second battery extends the life and less work (but to be fair, one screw using included driver, slide off plate, slide battery out, set to charge and reverse process to put battery back in. With two batteries, the whole thing takes about two minutes. With one, you simply have a non-functioning doorbell/camera for a few hours. No biggie, just FYI.
Also there is an an App called Neighbors free to join and use. It lets you share "videos and notifications of criminal or suspicious activity. So if someone in your neighborhood is broken into or home is vandalized they can share the video and/or share a notice of the incident. Lost dog, share. Delivery thieves, share. So both kinda cool and scary.
Now the BAD. To access the video you have to pay a monthly fee ( now if you access the video within the first 30 seconds or so, you are golden, but if you have your hands full, or can't access your phone, you can't see the video, or back it up. While the basic few is like $40 ish a year. Higher for the next tier up. That is forever. And no easy way to back up to a local storage device. All files are on Rings servers.
Now if you know that up front, and $40 is no biggie. Then 5 stars.
But for me that is an issue.
text_fidelity_b: Ring Video Doorbell 3 – enhanced wifi, improved motion detection, easy installation

VIVO Mobile TV Cart for 13 to 50 inch Screens up to 44 lbs, LCD LED OLED 4K Smart Flat and Curved Monitor Panels, Rolling Stand, Locking Wheels, Max VESA 200x200, Black, STAND-TV07W This Vivo Mobile TV Rolling Floor Stand is a tremendous value. It is strong steel, well finished and just right for rolling my 40" Vizio (which weighs only 17 lbs) around the patio for outdoor viewing at the optimal position and height. It looks great and functions flawlessly. It assembled easily. Though it comes with a sheetmetal wrench and a 4mm Allen, I used my own 8mm and 10mm sockets to speed assembly. And a 17mm end wrench to tighten the caster jam nuts. Sadly, one tiny nut was missing; I found a replacement from my personal metric collection of miscellaneous nuts and bolts. Pay close attention to the graphical instructions. I assembled the base upside down before realizing it was wrong. Easily remedied. Also comes with a collection of TV mounting screws, washers and spacers.

I was going to mount the TV on the wall, but being off to the side and quite high, that would very much limit viewing angles and no doubt strain necks. What I really wanted was to have the TV in front of me, wherever I might be sitting and also be able to optimize for group viewing if necessary.

This little cart is exactly what I wanted. It has 2" high quality urethane casters that roll effortlessly and silently on smooth surfaces. They aren't cheap hard plastic wheels. Each caster's threaded stem screws into a tapped hole. A jam nut on the threaded stem allows you to adjust the casters so all four are on the ground, then tighten the jam nuts to lock the adjustment. No wobble! You'll need a 17mm end wrench to tighten the nuts. Two of the casters are equipped with all-lock brakes that prevent both rolling and castering so the TV stays put if desired. When I'm done, I can simply roll the TV out of the way or into the house for safe storage.The base measures 18x20 inches. My 40" TV is 36" wide. You might think it would be top heavy or unstable, but it's not for me, especially as I have the mast set to near its lowest position.

The sturdy steel telescoping mast allows me to lower the TV so that the bottom edge of the 40" TV is 24" inches from the ground -- a few inches above coffee table height. This allows a very comfortable viewing angle when sitting in my somewhat lower patio chairs. In other words, it puts the TV at a very comfortable height to avoid neck strain.

The mount is adjustable and accommodates the 200x200mm Visa mount hole pattern on my TV. It can also handle 100x200 or smaller. Other stands have very large mounting bars. This one is small, simple and compact. Be aware its max Visa mount pattern is 200x200. You can adjust for level and tilt. It can tilt up about 15 degrees. It does not tilt down. The tilt is controlled by a knob. Be aware the TV is more or less permanently mounted onto the mast and the mast is bolted tightly to the base using five fasteners with locknuts: it does not come apart easily. If you want to disassemble this device for travel, you'll need to add thumbscrews.

I did not want extraneous things like extra shelves for a DVD player. It's clean and simple. Its price is very reasonable. With all the nuts and bolts tightened securely, there is no wobble anywhere.

Couldn't he happier. it's well engineered, strong, lightweight and portable.
text_fidelity_b: VIVO Mobile TV Cart for 13 to 50 inch Screens up to 44 lbs, LCD LED OLED 4K Smart Flat and Curved Monitor Panels, Rolling Stand, Locking Wheels, Max VESA 200x200, Black, STAND-TV07W

SamData 32GB USB Flash Drives 4 Pack 32GB Thumb Drives Memory Stick Jump Drive with LED Light for Storage and Backup (4 Colors: Black Blue Green Purple) If I could give these negative five stars, I would. These are a four-pack of 64GB thumb drives that come in four colors. The first color, black, that I plugged into the PC hopelessly causes the PC to stall and become unresponsive to the point where I have to pull the power cord out to get the machine to turn off.

I tried the purple one after that, and it worked. Removed it okay. I tried the next one and hopelessly unresponsive again. That's two bad thumb drives in a four-pack. I didn't bother trying the last one as I don't particularly appreciate yanking the power out of my PC like that.

Maybe SamData is trying to sound like SanDisk? I don't know. I know that two out of four bad drives in a single package are statistically impossible unless you're just selling bad drives like an everyday business model.

Someone out to look into this as it seems a lot like fraud to me. These drives may well damage your computer since I had to pull the plug to get my machine back with two out of the four drives from a single package.

Plantronics BackBeat PRO Wireless Noise Canceling Hi-Fi Headphones with Mic - Compatible with iPhone, iPad, Android, and Other Smart Devices I would, that I could give these headphones a zero-star rating. As I don’t think they deserve a whole star. When I was in school, a gold star meant something. And these headphones are not deserving of such.
Ok, on with the bad. My first set of these. If I would whipe the sweat out of my left ear. Left ear specifically, as the right ear did not produce this effect. The sound would cut off. Not the little off, then on again. As the phones shut off when you take them off your head. So a little off then on, would be expected. But I mean off, and stay that way. Then you need to turn off the headphones, with the switch, and back on again.
Which leads to the second problem. The phones cannot reconnect after the connection has been broken. The computer will blue screen, and restart. I thought, well maybe it is the Bluetooth receiver. So I got a new one, by a different company. Same issue.
Problem three. None of the buttons work. The buttons I am referring to are the play, pause, track forward, or track backward.
And it really makes me sad, to say these bad things about these phones. And I really tried to blame something other things at fault, to save their face. Because they have the most awesome form factor I can find in a headphone. The buttons are so intuitively placed, even if they do not work. The design, is obviously a different department. And the volume, is not controlled by a buttons. But rather a good old analog type knob. And the sound quality is pretty good, and also the noise cancelling works.
Oh yeah, I almost forgot. Because I really like the form factor. I thought I should give them another chance. So I replaced this set, with another set of the same model. And had the same problems. Evey, single, one, of them.

text_fidelity_a:
Sony XBR65X900F 65-Inch 4K Ultra HD Smart LED TV with $40 Off TV Wall Mount This TV makes me feel bad for ever having given another product 5 stars. It is really just about perfect. Instead of wasting a lot of space talking about the quality of the picture (believe me, it is there), I am going to concentrate on some finer points, particularly those real and perceived weak points:

(This is replacing a 2009 Sony Z-Series TV, which I also love and still consider a fantastic TV; it was the first year of Internet-capable TVs if I remember correctly, and I used the DLNA features with Universal Media Server, but could never get a Plex profile to work right, so I am happy to have a newer TV that supports Plex via App, besides for the 4k, HDR, etc., etc. I have a bunch of other TVs scattered about, but the other two I use most are less expensive Samsung Smart models from five or so years ago.)

Back to (possible) negatives:

I wasn't sure I would like the stand and style. I always hated those Samsung TVs with the plastic grey legs, and I thought this would look too much like that. I thought my ideal stand was either a perfect 90-degree version of the Sony A1E, or perhaps the A8F, which I had my eye on due to its very low profile, minimalist stand. Anyway, this one looks so much better in real life than I expected. It's actually metal, and fairly dark. Placed on low furniture, it looks great walking by, and sits at the right height while watching. I guess it is made to fit a Sony sound bar perfectly (I use full surround setup, so I don't care). But I am much, much happier with the looks than I thought I would be. If that is your hesitation, go check it out in a store (before coming back for the right price).

Thickness: its thicker than some, including last year's 930E, but the way it angles out from the back gives a much sleeker appearance than you may expect just from looking at the dimensions. You only see its thickness at about 80 degrees to the side. Overall, it sits back far and takes up little extra room than it has to. The TV looks as great off as it does on.

I read a professional review that mentioned the picture doesn't look as good from a side angle. I guess that's true, but it's not nearly as drastic of a change as it sounded from the review. In fact, one of the best TV seats in my house is about 30-degrees off-center, and I don't see a difference from there at all. At 45-degrees, you start to see a difference.

Above mentioned professional review also mentioned the Android TV thing can be a little clunky. I don't feel it, to be honest. It's been nothing but good surprises for me. One thing that could be improved is customization of your home screen. You can re-order some apps, but I haven't figured out how to delete the shortcuts for stuff that isn't even downloaded. And I'm never going to play goofy games on my TV (besides real video games), so how can I get rid of that whole section that is taking up space. You can block recommended content, so after them pushing some crapware on you initially, you can basically run add-free. Looks like you'll probably have to sign in to Google, though, but you can make a new account just for your TV (which is what I do for every device).

The downward facing ports look really good with the cable management, so good that I really don't want to use any of the side inputs for permanent setups. For that reason, they should have put the IR blaster and composite input facing down as well (not that I need them, as I don't have cable, but some people will).

Not that I even checked my link speed, but manual says Ethernet port is 100mbps. Can't imagine you'll ever need more than that unless you expect to run uncompressed video without a converter.

The remote is nicer than I expected, but still not as nice as my old one. Plus, although it has Bravia Sync, it doesn't easily just control my stereo the way I would like it to (as my old Sony TV did).Not sure why there has to be a Google button on the remote. Or even Netflix. These should be programmable. Actually, four programmable Apps and/or Input buttons would be greatly appreciated in their place.

That's about it for nitpicking. Here's some things that are totally awesome (besides all the obvious):

It can read all commonly used containers for video files, including *mkv, and it can decompress 4k HEVC (H.265) video natively. So even though my NAS cannot transcode 4k on the fly, if I set it to run at full quality, the TV does it just fine! And since H.265 was made because of 4k video, here's hoping we don't have formats this TV can't play any time soon. This is just fantastic to me, as I really love my NAS' Plex server function. You can also play up to 4k H.265 video right off a hard drive via USB.

My UMS media server is showing up under Video devices (which is where the DLNA servers show up), but you can't see the files. I haven't messed with it much (because now I don't care), but I assume they'll get a profile working before long.

I love the built-in TV guide function and also the way you can browse other channels along the bottom of your screen without changing the channel. These are both great features (the TV guide function on my old TV was abandoned after a few years, but I expect this one will continue to operate). I do not have or want cable, so now I have the features that are nice to have with cable without the burden of slow response cable boxes and the burden of dealing with Comcast.

I haven't even tried out the professional settings (or even messed with anything but motionflow) because the TV is impressing me every second it's on. Again, as this is the first 4k TV to reside in my house, I guess I should be amazed. But the blacks as bars on movies wider than 16:9 are so black you don't notice them. Space scenes are to die for. 4k is done right here: this is the high end of quality, about the only thing worth removing my old Z-series for. I just love it. It looks amazing on and off, and does everything I want it to do (mainly Plex, and Netflix is nice now and then as well). I'm so happy that Plex works so well with this TV without an expensive NAS upgrade, even with movies encoded at 2160p and 7.1 surround. Just fantastic.

It's better than I expected even from Sony's almost-second-to-flagship model. About as high end as they come before they jump up drastically in price. I wouldn't have anything less on my primary TV stand, and I don't need anything more. Highly recommended.
text_fidelity_b: Sony XBR65X900F 65-Inch 4K Ultra HD Smart LED TV with $40 Off TV Wall Mount

NEW Microsoft Surface Headphones 2 - Light Gray I'm not an audiophile, but I've tried out a good number of different earbud brands lately, all across the quality spectrum. I'm grading on a curve here.

Packaging is sufficient. A few tip sizes, quick start, instructions, and whatever is in that other manual of junk I always throw away. The earbud case is lozenge shaped and pocketable enough. No external lights, which is nice if you're charging it next to your bed, but not so much if you want to know their charge status.

They are supposed to immediately start trying to bluetooth pair with something when first opened, and appeared to be trying to do so. My Surface was unable to locate them. I even tried with a second Surface. I plugged in the case and left it to charge for 15 minutes, and then they paired fine. Overall on unboxing and setup, I'd say they're adequate, but far from exceptional.

The earbuds themselves are aggressively visible. I assume they're trying to ride the I-Pod branding success, but I'm not really feeling it. Despite looking huge, they don't feel huge. They are lightweight and comfortable. They don't feel like they are going to fall out, despite not feeling like they're crammed in the ear. Fit is unusual in that you can turn the earbud like a screw to make it tighter or looser. Sound is good. I'm giving them very low marks for appearance, and very good for fit and sound.

These use swipe style controls, which I despise. I much prefer a physical button that I can just feel that I've clicked. The controls do work as advertised, but there's enough delay that it often takes me a while of swiping my ear and waiting until it gets the message. Mostly irritating when someone tries to talk to me and I can't get it to pause for several seconds.

Range is average.

Overall, Id' say there's a bit of a brand name premium on the price compared to some other products, and I'm saying that as someone who has used Surface products as my primary computers for many years now, but they're not bad. I've definitely tried more expensive earbuds that weren't as good, but of what I've tried, I'm happiest so far with the Jabra Elite series of earbuds.

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech 3.5 mm Analog Stereo Headset H151 with Boom Microphone - Black, 7.9"x5.7"x2.4" Good crisp audio quality for phone calls. I like an on-the-ear headset instead of in-ear because cell phones have little or no sidetone.

Don't know what sidetone is? Back in the day, land line phone handsets fed the sound from the mic back into the earpiece, so a person could clearly monitor their own voice (and also hear any other sounds that the other party could hear that the mic picked up). That enabled a person to modulate their own voice (instead of screeching in order to hear themselves) and speak much more clearly. It made for a much better phone conversation experience. That feature was called sidetone.

It's a feature that cell phone designers and engineers somehow decided not to add to cell phones, or to make it so low in volume as to be nonexistent.

So until either cell phone engineers put sidetone back into cell phones or headset manufacturers start building it in as a feature, the workaround is on-ear headsets that allow you to hear your own voice while you speak.

The downside is that on-ear headsets aren't exactly convenient to carry around, and they're not inconspicuous. And they can be a bother if you're wearing a hat.

But they do give you some natural sidetone by allowing you to hear the sound of your voice. And this headset from Logitech, as I said, has some good crisp audio quality for phone calls.

Which brings up another point. Even after years of development, possibly the thing cell phones still do worst is make phone calls. The audio can still be garbled and fluttery due to digitizing and signals that fade in and out in strength. So good audio quality---in that mid-range EQ sweet spot---can make cell phone calls a lot more pleasant.

While there's a volume control on the cord, there's no answer button. That's probably a decision to keep the headset compatible with many devices.

Overall, good headset.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech 3.5 mm Analog Stereo Headset H151 with Boom Microphone - Black, 7.9"x5.7"x2.4"

He said it was near impossible with the way the house is built. This was my first time seeing 100 foot long ethernet cable--though, I confess, I never thought of looking for such a thing, or even knew they existed. 

He was able to run this directly from the router upstairs, and behind my living room sofa, down the stairway, alongside the wall and into the little room I have set up as an office and for shipping stuff-I've been sewing and shipping a lot of free masks this year. 

You can hardly tell this wire is even there. The little brackets they send with it, hold against the wall, and it's pulled so there's not much slack. You really have to pay close attention, just to see it. I'm so happy to have my pc up and running down there, so that I can stop running upstairs every time I need to print a label or download an embroidery design into one of my machines. 

I highly recommend these cables to anyone who likes to keep an old fashion pc, like me...or, you just need the internet in a far off place and need a super long cable.

text_fidelity_a:
Jiusion Telescope Eyepiece Plossl Eyepiece 32mm with 1.25inch Filter Threaded, Astronomical Telescope Lens 50% FOV increase at this price? This is the lowest priced Plössl I've ever seen and the reason for choosing it. Curiosity.

As a physicist with a too time-consuming career to fool around with optical Garage-a-Tronics projects, it's time for fun. After >40 years, I'd guess 1/3 of my time was in electro-optical systems. My responsibilities included one of the nation's most sophisticated optical design, fabrication, and 50-200 layers of Å thickness vapor deposition coating capability (200 layers is no limit … simply the most I've seen engineered)

You have to give them credit. Chinese optics are extraordinary and have been for 20 years. Asian pricing has wholly changed the marketplace. The crazy low prices have made complex systems affordable to the mass market. Optical grinding facilities remaining in the US are confined to a handful of custom, proto-typing houses run by old-timers with a decidedly different product application than consumer use.

The Plössl eyepiece is quite expensive to manufacture given the nature of the glass, coatings, and its precisely coordinated concave and convex lenses to neutralize internal reflections.

The Plössl has tradeoffs. All optical systems do. For example, Plössl's increased FOV comes with an eye relief confined to 70–80% of focal length.

Lenses are analog. Performance is not binary. 'Lowest price' in optics might be misunderstood. Optics lots begin production targeted at a spec performance that makes a profit. A production lot will yield a normal distribution to spec. On the upper end of the distribution are a few 'blue diamonds' commanding a super premium. Theoretically, 66%, will meet the target spec. Production lots begin life as profitable, spec-centered customers. 7% would be expected to fall short of some spec performance (i.e. start 107% of what you need) … Harvard MBA's demanding perfection in all things except stock value have never come to terms with normal analog distributions in scientific endeavors.

The lenses come without ref to detail specs, so I would believe the factory is emptying the shelves of sub-spec product here. Spec fallout, in my experience, may have little or nothing to do with operator perceptions of performance.

Excellent fun.

Was my review helpful? If so, click "Helpful" so I can know. Trying hard to put integrity into reviews
text_fidelity_b: Jiusion Telescope Eyepiece Plossl Eyepiece 32mm with 1.25inch Filter Threaded, Astronomical Telescope Lens
